verdict.reasoning: Patient says: "I've been having diarrhea for like, let's say, past three days, more or less."
Patient reports both duration and frequency: "it's been a very bad diarrhea... three days ago" and "around five to six times a day" and confirms "Yes, it's definitely watery. Loose stools? Yeah."
Patient: "it started like three days ago, and so it started with vomiting, so I vomited a couple of times, but then that went away. And, yeah, it's just diarrhea now."
Doctor: "Any blood in your stools?" Patient: "No, not that I could see."
Doctor: "have you noticed any other symptoms, like tummy pain?" Patient: "Not. Not really, no" – implies no significant abdominal pain.
Patient: "I feel like I can't really drink too much, so I feel very dehydrated."
Patient: "I'm trying to drink, but then I just go to the loo and I like, I. I poo everything and I feel dehydrated again." This supports that drinking is followed quickly by needing the bathroom.
Doctor asks about eating solids; patient: "Not much. Not much. So just a little bit" – indicates poor oral intake.
Patient continues: "but I don't feel. I don't really feel like I have appetite." which is reduced appetite.
On fever: Patient: "Probably at the beginning I was feeling. I had a bit of temperature, but now I feel. I feel kind of fine." This supports an initial mild fever.
Patient: "but now I feel. I feel kind of fine. I feel very weak, though." and denies current fever; implies now weak but not febrile.

Some systemic symptoms are discussed and denied (e.g., "Any headaches or muscle pains?" "Not really."), but the broad statement "no other systemic symptoms" generalizes beyond what was specifically asked in the transcript.
Patient: "So I do suffer of asthma" clearly confirms asthma history.

Patient on asthma treatment: "so I do have my nailers that I, you know, I use infrequently" and doctor clarifies "Is that a blue inhaler?" Patient: "Yes, it is." This implies an as-needed short-acting blue inhaler.
Doctor: "Do you have any allergies to any medications?" Patient: "Not that I know of." which corresponds to no known allergies.
Patient: "My father has high. Well, used to have high blood pressure." which is hypertension.
Patient: "He actually. So he actually died of bowel cancer like 10 years ago."
Patient: "Oh, yes. So probably it's worth mentioning she has diabetes." Doctor asks type; Patient: "It's type two."
Doctor: "Who lives at home with you, sir?" Patient: "Oh, I live alone."
Doctor: "What do you do for work?" Patient: "I'm a software engineer."
Doctor: "Have you taken time off work recently?" Patient: "Yes, yes, I have. These last three days I've been feeling really unwell, so I couldn't work." which is several days.
On alcohol: Patient: "I drink infrequently, like socially, let's say".
Patient: "and I don't smoke."
Doctor: "I think you're probably suffering from what we call gastroenteritis, okay. Which essentially is just a tummy bug."

Patient reports feeling dehydrated and poor intake; doctor emphasizes fluids: "You can drink plenty of fluids" and discusses fluid replacement due to losses. This supports concern for dehydration secondary to watery diarrhea and limited intake.
Asthma is mentioned ("I do suffer of asthma" and uses blue inhaler infrequently) but there is no explicit assessment statement that asthma is currently stable.

Doctor: "You can get things from the pharmacy, which called Diurelite, which can help replenish any minerals and vitamins you may have lost. It's a type of fluid replacement drink." This is an oral rehydration recommendation.
Doctor: "You can take some paracetamol if you're feeling feverish and weak."

Doctor: "Would probably advise you to continue taking time off work for next day or two until you get better. Normally you have to be diarrhea free for about 24 to 48 hours before you return back to work."
Doctor advises fluids and oral rehydration but does not specifically advise "eat small, tolerable solid foods"; eating solids is only queried, not recommended.
Doctor: "Let's see how the next few days go. And if you're still not better next week, I want you to come back and see me and we can have another look at your symptoms."
